description: The only thing the real ONNX checkpoints can be honestly benchmarked on in this repository: whether the registry config describes the checkpoint that is actually on disk. Model weights are fetched, never committed, so this suite cannot run in CI. It is a PLUMBING claim -- a graph whose tensors are named what the config says they are named is a graph the runtime can load, and nothing more. No accuracy, precision or recall number appears here or can, because there are no photographs to measure one on.
ci_exclusion_reason: needs models/weights populated by scripts/models/fetch_weights.py (190MB+, gitignored) and onnxruntime installed. Run: python3 -m memory_engine_eval.runner run --weights models/weights benchmarks/model-registry-graphs.suite.json

cases.measures: the fraction of claims the registry configs make about their ONNX graphs -- input tensor name, pinned spatial input size, every declared output name -- that the graph on disk agrees with, over only those checkpoints actually present
cases.does_not_measure: whether any of these models detects a face, embeds an image or scores quality; a correctly named tensor says the config matches the file and says nothing else

falsifications.why: claiming an input tensor the graph does not have is exactly the drift this case exists to catch -- a config edited past its checkpoint -- and it must not agree

issue #36 was SCRFD with the wrong output names in its config, which produced a detector that merely seemed mediocre; renaming every declared output must collapse the agreement. The bound is 0.9 rather than the 0.23 measured against four checkpoints because which checkpoints are on a machine decides how many claims there are, and a bound tuned to one machine's weights directory is a bound that fails on another
